answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying earning power to verifiable work history instead of raw account count. Each agent stakes a small bond before taking paid jobs; honest completion grows its reputation like a lotus rising through murky water, while fraud forfeits the bond. New identities start on a narrow ledge — limited to tiny, supervised tasks — and only climb to bigger work after a proven record. An umber ledger of signed past behavior makes fresh fake agents expensive and pointless, since reputation cannot be cloned.
